items.title: [TTTv2] Four pre-existing defects in models/common surfaced by the tier-1 CI migration: attention decode PCC, Sampling1DConfig.local_indices, rmsnorm tolerance, load_tensor SIGBUS
items.body:
## Summary

Migrating the TTTv2 module suites into the tiered Models CI pipelines (#53911) ran them under conditions the T3K pipelines never applied — a forced watcher, a read-only `/mnt/MLPerf`, and a cold tensor cache. That surfaced four distinct pre-existing defects in `models/common`, plus one infrastructure gap. None is caused by the migration; all are reproducible on `main`.

This issue collects them so they can be split into per-owner fixes. Two of them currently make the TT-Transformers tier-1 unit gate red on landing.

Evidence throughout is from run [32516753713](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32516753713) on `wh_llmbox`, with `/mnt/MLPerf` mounted read-write and no watcher, against a `tt_cache/tttv2/attention_1d` regenerated from empty. Results were byte-identical to run [32510125078](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32510125078), so these are deterministic, not flakes.

Per-module results in that run:

| Module | Result |
|---|---|
| `models/common/tests` (non-module) | 1 failed / 1718 passed / 248 skipped |
| mlp | 28 passed |
| rmsnorm | 27 passed |
| rope | 42 passed |
| lm_head | 13 passed |
| **attention** | **16 failed** / 24 passed / 14 skipped |
| embedding | 19 passed |
| penalties | 81 passed |
| **sampling** | **71 failed** / 53 passed |

---

## A · `Sampling1DConfig` is missing `local_indices` — 71 failures

`models/common/modules/sampling/sampling_1d.py:194`, in `load_device_buffers()`:

```python
self._local_indices = _materialize(cfg.local_indices)
```

`Sampling1DConfig` (same file, lines 53-90) does not declare that field, so this raises:

```
AttributeError: 'Sampling1DConfig' object has no attribute 'local_indices'
```

`release()` reads the same name via `getattr(self.config, name, None)`, so only the load path dies.

**This is a half-applied revert, not a missing field.** #53001 (`b915f58d5f0`, 08-17) removed the iota `local_indices` buffer wholesale — it was the subject of #52928, where `ttnn.topk` received an `indices_tensor` half the width of the logits and returned indices that did not match the values beside them. #51184 (`310f9ef60fa`, 08-19) rewrote `load_device_buffers()` to add `try`/`release()` handling and carried the deleted reader back with it.

State on `main`:

| Piece | State |
|---|---|
| `Sampling1DConfig.local_indices` field | deleted by #53001 |
| its builder (`_make_local_indices`, `to_set["local_indices"]`) | deleted by #53001 |
| `required_buffers` (line 105) | correct — no `local_indices` |
| reader `cfg.local_indices` (line 194) | resurrected → `AttributeError` |
| `_topk_single_device` slice + `ttnn.split` (574-577) | resurrected; the resulting `indices_list` is never used |
| `_topk_multi_device` slice + `indices_tensor=local_indices` (619-627) | resurrected |

**Re-adding the field is the wrong direction** — it reinstates the buffer #53001 deliberately dropped, and the builder is gone anyway. The fix is to finish that removal: drop the line 194 reader, the dead slice/split in `_topk_single_device`, and the slice plus `indices_tensor=` argument in `_topk_multi_device`, letting `ttnn.topk` generate the index tile itself. #53001 verified that bit-identical to the iota buffer at twelve widths, across both program factories and the UINT16→UINT32 boundary. Four deletions, roughly a dozen lines, nothing added.

One caveat: #53001 only ever fixed the single-device path — its own notes record 1×2 measuring zero mismatches and 1×8 / 4×8 unmeasured — so dropping `indices_tensor=` on the multi-device path is new ground and wants a run behind it.

---

## B · Attention decode-path PCC failures — 16 failures

`models/common/tests/modules/attention/test_attention_1d.py`, PCC as low as **0.1498**:

```
FAILED test_attention_1d_vs_reference[10-standard-1x{1,2,8}-decode-32-{1B,8B0,11B}-…]
FAILED test_attention_1d_vs_reference[10-paged-1x{1,2,8}-decode-32-{1B,8B0,11B}-…]
FAILED test_attention_1d_prefill_decode_transition[{paged,non-paged}-1x{1,2,8}]
FAILED test_attention_prefill_selects_scalar_or_tensor_chunk_start_api[{True,False}]
```

Observed PCC values span 0.1498 – 0.66 against passing cases at 1.0.

Notable characteristics:

- **Every failure is on the decode path** (`-decode-32-`) or the prefill→decode transition. Prefill-only cases pass.
- Affects **1×1, 1×2 and 1×8** alike, so not mesh- or CCL-specific.
- Affects **Llama 1B, 8B and 11B** — models *without* Q/K bias. `models/common/tests/modules/attention/low_pcc_notes.md` documents a HuggingFace-vs-Meta RoPE permutation of the Q/K **bias** as a known degradation source, but that mechanism requires a bias and does not apply here. So this is not the documented case.
- **Not cache-related.** Reproduced identically against a `tt_cache/tttv2/attention_1d` deleted and regenerated from empty, with the mount read-write so nothing fell back.
- **Not watcher-related.** No watcher active; zero watcher events in the log.
- Deterministic: identical counts and 3:57 duration across two independent runs.

This one I could not attribute to a specific commit and I do not believe it is tracked elsewhere. It is the highest-value item here — a decode-path PCC of 0.15 means wrong output, not marginal drift.

---

## C · `test_validation_rmsnorm_host_and_device[1x1]` tolerance failure — 1 failure

```
max_abs_error=3.125000e-02 exceeds tolerance 1.000000e-02
```

`models/common/tests/test_validation_tools.py`. Pre-existing on `main` — the same single failure appears in the `t3k_tttv2_fast_unit_tests` job on `main` ([run 32489962502](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32489962502)). Either a real regression or a tolerance that needs revisiting; it is the only failure in the 1719-case non-module suite.

---

## D · `all_gather_async` assert — already tracked

Running the attention suite under `TT_METAL_WATCHER=30` reproduces **G1 of #50886** / #49081: exit 134, watcher assert in the `minimal_default_reader` NCRISC kernel, fabric EDM router hang, on the 8-chip mesh. Recorded on both issues already; noted here only for completeness. It is invisible with the watcher off, which is how the migrated entries now run.

---

## E · Infrastructure: `ttnn.load_tensor` raises `SIGBUS` on an unreadable cache entry

Not a `models/common` bug, but it cost significant triage time and is cheap to improve.

`tt_cache/tttv2/attention_1d` had been seeded in February 2026 and never refreshed. Reading one of those entries killed the process outright:

```
Fatal Python error: Bus error
  File ".../ttnn/operations/core.py", line 588 in load_tensor
  File "/work/models/common/modules/lazy_weight.py", line 121 in get_device_weight
```

The file was complete and correctly sized (295,272 bytes = 32 × 4608 × 2 + header) and the export had 7.3 TB free, so neither truncation nor space explains it — the mapping simply extends past what the file can serve. Because `SIGBUS` is uncatchable, there is no error message naming the file, and the failure is indistinguishable from a device fault.

Validating the header against the on-disk size before mapping would turn this into a diagnosable error. Related: a partially-written entry left behind by an aborted run produces the same signature, which makes any interrupted cache-population run silently poisonous to later ones.

---

## Suggested split

1. **B** — attention decode PCC. Wrong output, untracked, blocks the attention gate.
2. **A** — `local_indices`. Understood, four deletions, blocks the sampling gate. Needs a multi-device run to confirm.
3. **C** — tolerance failure, isolated.
4. **E** — `load_tensor` size validation, diagnosability only.
5. **D** — already tracked in #49081.

A and B are what make the TT-Transformers tier-1 unit entries red in #53911. That PR registers them per module, so each failure is attributable to one job rather than reddening the whole set, and it does not attempt to fix or mask either.

items.title: Blaze pipeline: intermittent decoder-output PCC~0 on Kimi-K2.6 padded chunked prefill (no-trace, dense path)
items.body:
### Summary

`Kimi-K2.6-1T chunked prefill padded accuracy 15k@5k (no trace) [bh_sc1]` intermittently returns **uncorrelated decoder output** (`decoder-output min PCC -0.001204 < 0.88`) on the blaze prefill pipeline, on current main-era bases. Kimi-K2.6 is **dense MLA** (no DSA indexer), so this is a dense-path correctness flap.

### Evidence

Across four dispatches of the pipeline on two branches whose diffs are provably unreachable from Kimi's graph (dense model; the branch only touches the DSA indexer path) plus pristine main:

| run | Kimi padded accuracy (no trace) |
|---|---|
| [branch run 1](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32382113328) | FAIL (job summary shows test passed once on retry, job failed in post-step) |
| [main control](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32386664431) | flapped attempt-1, recovered on retry |
| [branch targeted-2](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32434028112) | **FAIL — PCC -0.0012** |
| [branch targeted-3](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32440047786) | flapping across attempts |

The trace variant of the same test is consistently green — because the traced harness asserts **KV-cache PCC only**, while the no-trace variant additionally PCCs each layer's decoder output (`test_prefill_transformer_chunked.py` "UNTRACED ONLY" block). i.e. the corruption hits hidden states while leaving the KV stem intact, and trace lanes are structurally blind to it.

### Suspects

Intermittent + padded-path + recent onset points at the recent main window: `ttnn.pad` rank>4 change (#52870) or the 2026-08-19/20 UMD bumps. The same window also shows a ~20% no-trace perf regression on the Kimi chunked perf lane (host-dispatch-bound path; possibly the same cause or the documented per-chunk variance).

### Why this matters

An intermittent PCC≈0 on a dense production model's accuracy lane both (a) masks real regressions via retry-to-green, and (b) suggests a live correctness hazard in padded chunked prefill. Worth a bisect over the suspect window on a quiet `bh_sc1` machine.

items.title: [TT-NOP-Injector][WH] mismatch race on eltwise_binary dest_reuse
items.body:
Sub-issue of #53394 (TT-NOP injector tool race findings - LLK).

## Summary

Wormhole `DEST_TO_SRCA` Elwmul dest-reuse mismatches when unpack sync is delayed.

**Deterministic:** two full `1-100` sweeps,  Same 8 variants mismatched both times

| site | addr | source | NOP | failing n |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unpack:2 `STALLWAIT` | `0x05a28` | `llk_unpack_AB.h:274` `TTI_STALLWAIT(STALL_UNPACK, TRISC_CFG)` | `unpacr1` | 12 |
| unpack:2 `STALLWAIT` | `0x05a28` | `llk_unpack_AB.h:274` | `unpacr0` | 14 |
| unpack:2 `STALLWAIT` | `0x05a28` | `llk_unpack_AB.h:274` | `tti_nop` | 30, 33 |
| unpack:2 `STALLWAIT` | `0x05a28` | `llk_unpack_AB.h:274` | `risc_nop` | 30, 33 |
| unpack:3 `SEMGET` | `0x05a30` | `ckernel.h:319` `TTI_SEMGET` via `llk_unpack_AB.h:280` `t6_semaphore_get(UNPACK_SYNC)` | `unpacr1` | 13 |
| unpack:3 `SEMGET` | `0x05a30` | `ckernel.h:319` / `llk_unpack_AB.h:280` | `unpacr0` | 15 |

Math thread had no recorded misses. Kernel: `eltwise_binary_test.cpp:69` `run_kernel` → `_llk_unpack_AB_`.

## Recreate

Branch: [`nmohammed/timing-perturbations-tt-llk`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/tree/nmohammed/timing-perturbations-tt-llk)

```bash
cd tt_metal/tt-llk/tests/python_tests/ttnop

# STALLWAIT @ llk_unpack_AB.h:274 — tti_nop 30,33 (also risc_nop 30,33; unpacr1 12; unpacr0 14)
CHIP_ARCH=wormhole ./focus.sh --site sync --sites unpack:2 --nop tti_nop \
  --delays 30,33 --repeats 5 \
  'test_eltwise_binary.py::test_eltwise_binary_dest_reuse[reuse_dest_type:DEST_TO_SRCA-math_op:Elwmul-formats:Float32->Float32-math_fidelity:HiFi3-tile_dimensions:[16, 32]-input_dimensions:[512, 32]-output_dimensions:[128, 32]]'

```

items.title: global_avg_pool2d returns structurally wrong values on Blackhole for [1,7,7,2048] (PCC 0.55)
items.body:
## Summary

`test_run_average_pool[BFLOAT16-resnet50_unpadded]` fails its correlation check on Blackhole:

```
Passing PCC = False
Output PCC = 0.5478098686296509
```

`tests/tt_eager/python_api_testing/unit_testing/misc/test_average_pool.py::test_run_average_pool`, `act_shape = [1, 7, 7, 2048]`, `bfloat16`.

The value is bit-identical across runs, so this is deterministic rather than flaky. The sibling parameterisation in the same file (`tile_divisible`, `[1, 1, 32, 64]`) passes at PCC 0.9999984714740633, so `global_avg_pool2d` is not broken in general — it is specific to this shape.

## The output is structurally wrong, not mis-scaled

Worth stating up front because it rules out the obvious explanation. `shape_padded()` pads dim 2 from 7 to 32, so the tensor handed to the op is `[1, 7, 32, 2048]` with 25 zero columns, while the golden is computed on the unpadded `[1, 7, 7, 2048]`. If the op simply averaged over the padded extent, every channel would be scaled by the same 49/224 = 0.21875 and PCC would stay at 1.0, because Pearson correlation is scale-invariant.

Measured per-channel ratio of output to golden:

```
ratio   mean=2.263587   std=116.446693   min=-1134.297852   max=5111.541504
```

Individual channels also flip sign:

```
first 8 out    : -0.00800  -0.03809  -0.08887  +0.07910  +0.08301  -0.08398  -0.01746  +0.03418
first 8 golden : -0.06395  -0.02713  -0.12696  -0.00901  -0.13661  -0.18339  -0.08714  +0.10446
```

So the result is not the correct answer times a constant. Something in the padded path produces different values per channel.

## Reproduction

```bash
pytest tests/tt_eager/python_api_testing/unit_testing/misc/test_average_pool.py \
  -k "BFLOAT16-resnet50_unpadded" -xvvv
```

(or `scripts/run_safe_pytest.sh --run-all tests/tt_eager/python_api_testing/unit_testing/misc/test_average_pool.py -v`, which runs both parameterisations and shows the passing sibling alongside.)

## What has been ruled out

- **Not flaky.** Same PCC to the last digit across every run.
- **Not a scale/normalisation error.** Per-channel ratios vary by orders of magnitude and change sign (above).
- **Not DRAM harvesting.** The system this was found on has one GDDR channel harvested per chip; the test returns `0.5478098686296509` with 7 banks and the identical value with all 8 banks enabled, with no other change.
- **Not the op in general.** The tile-aligned parameterisation passes at 0.9999998.

## Possible direction

The one structural difference between the failing and passing cases is that the failing one goes through `pad_to_tile(0.0)`. Note that dim 2 here is a spatial dimension (the tensor is NHWC, so `[N, H, W, C]` and W is padded 7 to 32), and zero-padding a spatial dimension is not a no-op for average pooling. Whether the defect is that the op mishandles the padded region, or that padding metadata is not carried into the reduction, I have not determined — flagging it as the obvious place to look rather than as a diagnosis.

## Related

[#44002](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/44002) is the same test in the same CI group, but a different symptom — a hard `TT_FATAL` about tile alignment after `global_avg_pool2d`, fixed and closed in May. This is a wrong-results failure, not a crash, so it is a separate problem on the same test.

[#6237](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/6237) reported low PCC from `global_avg_pool2d` on Grayskull and is closed. No open issue matches low PCC on Blackhole.

## Environment

Blackhole, firmware 19.13.2, KMD 2.9.0. The test carries no architecture-specific handling, so it is expected to pass here.

items.title: [tt-train] sdpa_fw hangs with AttentionMaskType::None; WH fw/bw softmax-scale mismatch; sdpa_bw validation gaps and NaN on fully-masked rows
items.body:
Found in a systematic audit of tt-train's fused metal kernels.

## Bug 1: `sdpa_fw` with `AttentionMaskType::None` deadlocks

`sdpa_fw_compute_kernel.cpp:194-224` — the `#else` branch (mask_type == None) unconditionally calls `apply_mask_on_reg(matmul_accum_reg, cb_attn_mask, ...)` (:212) and `cb_pop_front(cb_attn_mask, Sk_chunk_t)` (:223), but for None:

- the host never creates CB c_3 (`sdpa_fw_program_factory.cpp:401` guards on `mask_type != None`),
- the reader never reads mask tiles (all mask reads under `#ifdef USE_ATTN_MASK`),
- the writer only generates causal tiles under CAUSAL/BALANCED.

`apply_mask_on_reg` does `cb_wait_front` on a CB that is never configured or pushed → hang or garbage. Validation accepts None (`sdpa_fw_device_operation.cpp:128-136`); the host comment ("kernel will just scale attention scores", factory:520) shows the no-mask path was intended but never implemented. The bw kernels do this correctly (`sdpa_bw_q_compute_kernel.cpp:152-155` has a proper scale-only `#else`).

**Trigger:** any `metal::sdpa_fw(..., None, ...)` call — exactly what the ring-attention merge simulation test does (`sdpa_bw_op_test.cpp:1137,1225`); that test is GTEST_SKIPped, so zero coverage. Fix is a 2-line `#ifdef USE_ATTN_MASK` guard.

## Bug 2: fw/bw softmax-scale mismatch on Wormhole

`sdpa_compute_utils_common.hpp:174,189` — the WH path of `sdpa_exp_tile_scaled` uses `scaler_bf16 = (uint16_t)(scaler_fp32 >> 16)`: a bf16 **truncation** (not round-to-nearest) of the scale. So fw computes P with the bf16 scale, but fw's LSE uses the full fp32 scale (`compute_and_pack_lse`, `sdpa_compute_utils.hpp:459-461`) and bw recomputes P = exp(scale_fp32·s − lse) with the fp32 scale (`sdpa_bw_compute_utils.hpp:61`). For head dims where 1/√d is not bf16-exact (d=128: rel. error ~2⁻⁹; d=64 is exact, masking this in most tests), bw's recomputed P deviates from fw's actual P by several percent on low-probability entries — a systematic fw/bw inconsistency biasing dS. BH is unaffected (fp32 scale in LREG12). Plausibly part of why D=128 bw configs need 3e-2 tolerances.

## Bug 3: bw host validation gaps → silent gradient corruption

- **dtype never pinned to BF16:** both bw factories size all CBs with `bfloat16_single_tile_size_bytes` but set data_format from the actual dtype (`sdpa_bw_q_program_factory.cpp:252-254,327-351`); validation only checks dtypes are equal to each other. FLOAT32 inputs → 4KB tiles in 2KB pages → garbage. fw validates BF16 explicitly.
- **`intermediates` completely unvalidated** in both bw ops — must be the fw (B,H,S,32) FP32 lse tensor; reader assumes FP32 tile size. Wrong tensor → silent garbage gradients.
- **dropout silently ignored in bw** (fw TT_FATALs on dropout≠0; bw accepts and ignores).
- No tile-alignment validation: `scaler = 1/√(padded qEmbd)` (`sdpa_fw_program_factory.cpp:271,293-294`) — logical head_dim 40 → padded 64 → wrong scale, no error.

## Bug 4: fully-masked rows (Arbitrary mask) → uniform attention in fw, inf/NaN in bw

fw masks by adding −1e9 before the row-max reduce, so a fully-masked row gets exp(scale·(s−max))=1 everywhere → output = mean(V), lse ≈ −1e8. bw computes P = exp(scale·s − lse) = exp(+1e8) = inf on any position not masked identically — and bw uses true −inf (`hal::get_inf()`, `sdpa_bw_q_program_factory.cpp:279`) vs fw's −1e9, a second fw/bw asymmetry. Padding masks that fully mask a row (padded batches) hit NaN gradients. No test covers this.

## Context: backward is effectively unverified

10 of 12 bw accuracy tests are DISABLED_ citing #46121 (non-deterministic accuracy failures); the only always-on passing bw test is B=1, S=32, single core, single tile. The two largest fw causal tests (the only ones exercising balanced parallelism + Sk_chunk_t=4 with the packer-L1-accumulate mask stamp) are also disabled. GQA, causal, and diff-vdim gradients should be treated as unknown-correct until #46121 is root-caused.

2. Pin bw dtypes, validate intermediates, TT_FATAL on dropout≠0 in bw, TT_FATAL on padded≠logical dims.
